topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets out the core themes of cancer causation, and outlines the learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Intrinsic and Extrinsic Factors in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental nature of cancer as a genetic disease and assess the relative contributions of random endogenous mutations, environmental exposures, and epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Biological, Chemical, and Physical Carcinogenic Agents
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific infectious, dietary, radiant, and chemical agents, focusing on the biochemical and metabolic pathways that generate DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Context
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, contrasting tumor initiators with promoters and highlighting the influence of chronic inflammation and host developmental timing.

topics.label: Methods for Assessing and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic signatures, epidemiological approaches, and experimental assays used to establish carcinogenic risk and identify causative agents.
